note: A beginner's week of three practice days, about 40 minutes each, in the current teaching style: every step says what is on the screen, where a run starts, which way it goes and where it turns, and no step names a scale position by a bare number. Each day opens with a warm-up and ends in something made up or a tune; days 2 and 3 each hold a mix exercise (seven open chords in any order, major and minor triads in one key). The A minor pentatonic scale returns on all three days in a new form: phrases, a riff, down-up picking and a jam over two chords.

plan.title: Week 1: a first scale, chords in time and chords made smaller
plan.summary: Three practice days of about 40 minutes. Day 1 is the A minor pentatonic scale and the G, C and D chords in time. Day 2 makes chords smaller, as power chords and triads, and mixes all seven open chords. Day 3 adds down-up picking and a strumming pattern, mixes major and minor triads, and ends with a jam over two chords.
plan.progress:
Techniques: the spider is clean at frets 5 to 8 in the orders 1-2-3-4 and 1-3-2-4 at a slow tempo. Next: the spider from the 1st fret, where the frets are wider.
Basic chords: G, C, D and Em change in time with down strums; all seven open chords were met in mixed orders, and the island strum on G, Em, C and D is new. A5, D5 and E5 are played as power chords. Next: the island strum at a faster tempo, and power chords with the root on other frets.
Scales: the A minor pentatonic scale from the root on the low E string, with down-up picking, phrases that end on the root, a two-note riff and a jam over Am and G landing on chord notes. Next: the same scale in E, then the position next to it.
CAGED: G, C and D as triads on the top three strings, one shape moved and three shapes in one place; the minor triads of G major were met in the mix. Next: the same triads one set of strings lower.
